curriculum.title: Stephen and the Gospel Beyond Jerusalem

core.big_idea: Opposition did not stop the witness to Jesus and helped carry the gospel outward.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate context; select age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Acts and the expanding church within Church, Scripture and Christian Hope

claims.statement: The selected passage supplies the principal textual evidence for Stephen and the Gospel Beyond Jerusalem.
Opposition did not stop the witness to Jesus and helped carry the gospel outward.

core.interpretation_skill: Identify context and sequence; distinguish direct description from inference and application

learning.foundation_objective: Explain from the passage that opposition did not stop the witness to jesus and helped carry the gospel outward and locate the lesson on the whole-Bible timeline.
learning.extension_objective: Identify the immediate context and genre, then distinguish what the text directly states from a reasonable inference and application.
know: Opposition did not stop the witness to Jesus and helped carry the gospel outward.
The lesson belongs in Acts and the expanding church within Church, Scripture and Christian Hope.
understand: Direct observation must remain distinct from interpretation, synthesis, framework position, and application.
practise: Retell or analyse the passage using evidence from the text.
Name one faithful response without claiming more than the passage supports.
become: A learner who responds to Scripture with trust, wisdom, worship, service, repentance, or love as appropriate.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage.
Student can support the big idea with evidence.
Student can distinguish observation from interpretation or application.

text_observations: The selected passage supplies the principal textual evidence for Stephen and the Gospel Beyond Jerusalem.

interpretation_notes: Start with the selected passage before moving to synthesis or application.
Read this as Acts narrative and account for its immediate literary setting.
Distinguish explicit text, synthesis, inference, framework position, and prudential application.
theological_guardrails: Do not romanticise persecution or imply suffering proves spiritual superiority.
Keep Stephen's death age-appropriate and avoid graphic detail.

family.title: Family Bible Time: Stephen and the Gospel Beyond Jerusalem
family.parent_intro: In about 15 minutes, read Acts 6:8-8:4 and explore this big idea: Opposition did not stop the witness to Jesus and helped carry the gospel outward.

flow.instructions: Recall where Stephen and the Gospel Beyond Jerusalem fits in the Bible story.
Read or retell Acts 6:8-8:4 and notice two details.
Ask what the passage directly says and what meaning follows from it.
Use the Stephen and the Gospel Beyond Jerusalem Evidence Grid orally or on paper.
Choose one voluntary response and pray together.

questions: What happened or what was taught?

family.parent_note: Questions are welcome. Do not force disclosure, certainty, public prayer, baptism, or another public religious decision.

quiz.question: Which passage is central to Stephen and the Gospel Beyond Jerusalem?
quiz.explanation: The lesson is governed by its principal passage.

quiz.question: Which reading habit is most responsible?
options: Observe context and genre before concluding.
Start with the application you want.
Treat every narrative detail as a command.

answer.text: Observe context and genre before concluding.

quiz.explanation: Observation and context precede synthesis and application.

quiz.question: Opposition did not stop the witness to Jesus and helped carry the gospel outward.
quiz.explanation: This is the governed big idea for the lesson.

quiz.question: Should an inference be described as explicit text when the passage does not state it directly?
quiz.explanation: Inference and direct wording must remain distinct.

accessibility.reading_level: Upper-primary guided reading with concrete supports
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Define unfamiliar terms before theological shorthand.
neurodiversity_supports: Allow students to pass on personal-sharing questions.
non_reader_support: Read aloud and use icons, sequence cards, oral choices, or a scribe.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of trauma, family finances, grief, abuse, or private spiritual decisions.
Do not pressure a child or young person toward baptism, public prayer, or another public response.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Use the lesson guardrails in the review sheet; answer from the evidence, avoid coercion, and route personal or safety concerns to appropriate adults.
